```{r setup}
library(glass.sqdaitools)
```

This vignette walks through the GLASS data lifecycle covered by the package:
registry lookups, tile mapping, DOY folders, downloading and post-processing.
Dataset-bound chunks run offline; anything that touches the network is shown
with `eval = FALSE` so the vignette builds without connectivity.

## The product registry

The registry has one row per archive variant (product x source x resolution)
observed under <https://glass.hku.hk/archive/>:

```{r}
glass_registry(verified_only = TRUE)[, c("variant_id", "res", "cadence_days",
                                         "observed_years", "url_root")]
```

Variants with `verified = TRUE` were checked against real granules: file
naming fragments (`code`, `version`, `layer`), year coverage, and band
metadata (`fill_value`, `scale_factor`, `valid_min/valid_max`) all come from
that check and are consumed by `glass_read()`/`glass_process()`.

## From region of interest to tiles

Tiled GLASS products reuse the MODIS sinusoidal `h<v>` grid. Rebuild the
exact tile polygons and see which ones your study area needs:

```{r}
# 一个 2-3 km 缓冲的点(上海人民广场周边)
roi <- sf::st_buffer(
  sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(121.47, 31.23)), crs = 4326),
  3000
)
tiles <- glass_tiles_for_sf(roi)
tiles[, c("h", "v", "lon_min", "lon_max", "lat_min", "lat_max", "valid")]
```

For straight bounding boxes there is `glass_tiles_for_bbox()`, and passing
the resulting table directly to `glass_fetch()` is allowed (it understands
data frames with `h`/`v` columns).

## Date range to composite folders

The archive stores one folder per composite start day-of-year:

```{r}
glass_doys("LAI_MODIS_250M", from = "2018-08-01", to = "2018-08-31")
```

`mode = "span"` (default) keeps composites partially overlapping the range;
`mode = "start"` keeps only those starting inside it.

## Finding and downloading files

`glass_list_files()` reads one composite folder's listing; `glass_fetch()`
loops it over the DOY table and downloads with resume/verification:

```{r eval=FALSE}
files <- glass_fetch(
  "LAI_MODIS_250M",
  from = "2018-08-01", to = "2018-12-31",
  roi = roi,
  out_dir = "data/glass/lai"
)
# 用 dry_run = TRUE 先看清单,不下载
```

The download engine compares sizes with the server, resumes `.part` files
via HTTP `Range`, and writes `glass_manifest.csv` into `out_dir`, so an
interrupted run continues where it stopped.

## Post-processing

`glass_process()` is the parameterised pipeline: cleanup, mosaic, reproject,
mask, optional temporal collapse:

```{r eval=FALSE}
mean_lai <- glass_process(
  files,
  roi = roi,
  product = "LAI_MODIS_250M",
  method = "cubic",
  fun = "mean",
  outfile = "glass_lai_mean.tif"
)
```

Band cleanup comes from the registry: the raw fill (e.g. 255) maps to `NA`
after scaling, and the valid scaled range is excluded from analysis. For an
already-read `SpatRaster`, `glass_read()` with no `product` is a no-op
except for explicit `fill`/`valid_range` arguments.

## Interactive UI

```{r eval=FALSE}
glass_app()
```

Draw the ROI on a map, pick a verified variant, preview the manifest and
download — the same package functions underneath. The output folder can be
chosen through the built-in, in-page directory browser (or typed directly)
and a progress bar follows each file during the batch download.
